title: feat: computer MCP (persistent per-user filesystem + bash)
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
**What:** every Pollinations user gets a private, persistent computer as a builtin MCP server (`/mcp/computer`): a filesystem plus a bash shell that survive between agent runs.

- Adds `apps/computer-mcp`: a private Worker on `@cloudflare/computer`. One Durable Object per user holds the files; bash (just-bash) runs in a throwaway Worker. Coreutils, grep, sed, awk, jq, tar, curl, git.
- One tool, `bash`: `command`, optional `stdin` (file content for `cat > path`, no quoting), optional `cwd` (default `/workspace`, created if missing; projects are folders).
- In: `curl -o` any public URL, `git clone` any public repo. Out: `assets publish <path>` copies a file to the media service and prints its unlisted URL (`MEDIA` service binding, same as ffmpeg-mcp), or `git push` to a repo the user owns with their token in the remote URL. The service mints no credentials and shares nothing between users.
- Memory is a convention, not a tool: a seeded `/workspace/README.md` tells the agent to keep `memory/facts.md` and a dated `memory/log/`.
- Billing: flat 0.0002 Pollen per successful call via usage receipt; storage and discovery free.
- Wiring: registry entry `computer` (enter's agent form picks it up), `COMPUTER_MCP` service binding in gen, docs section, tests.

Alternative on #14742: same wiring, upstream Code Mode example instead of a bash tool.

Staging Worker deployed; production only via `Deploy / Cloudflare production` after promotion. Needs a paid Workers plan (`worker_loaders`).

gist.headline: A computer for every bee
gist.blurb: Agents can now keep a little private workshop between runs: files stay put, bash does the chores, and no one has to pretend a README is long-term memory. The new built-in computer MCP brings a persistent workspace to the hive.
gist.summary: Added the built-in `/mcp/computer` MCP server, giving every user a private persistent filesystem and a `bash` tool with core utilities, public `curl`/`git clone`, asset publishing, and authenticated pushes to their own repositories.
gist.impact: Agents can now carry projects, notes, and generated files across runs in a per-user `/workspace`, then publish assets or push completed work to repositories the user owns.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy shared-but-private garden workshop represents the per-user computer: Polli tends a labeled workspace planter where code-files and memory notes grow permanently, while a small retro terminal runs bash commands. A file cabinet, shell prompt, tiny git branch, and an asset crate headed toward a glowing public URL sign represent persistent files, repository work, and publishing; the scene should make the workspace feel safe, personal, and useful.
